title: Free a riser that is sitting on a pencil, without spilling the open jar on it
instruction: The riser under the open glass jar of varnish is sitting on a pencil. Get the riser flat on the table where it is, keeping the jar standing on it without spilling.
context: A stand set down on a stray pencil, screw or offcut looks placed but is tilted, and whatever is on it is not safe to work from. The debris is pinned by the load: pulling at it drags the stand and its load along rather than freeing it, so one hand takes the weight off that side while the other clears the debris, and the stand is checked for sitting on all four corners before work goes on.
setup: Six loose objects on the table. Positions are (x, y) in cm: x forward from the line joining the two arm bases, y to the left of the midline between the arms (the bases are at y = +30.5 and -30.5). Task objects: (1) Dark-stained oak riser, a solid block 26 x 7 x 4 cm, 0.50 kg, lying on its 26 x 7 cm face with its long side pointing straight away from the arms, centred at (27, 0): near end at x = 14, far end at x = 40. (2) Yellow wooden pencil, 17.5 cm long, 7 mm across, 6 g, lying at right angles to the riser at x = 25, from y = -2 to y = -19.5, so its tip is 1.5 cm under the riser's right-hand long edge and the other 16 cm sticks out to the right. (3) Open glass jar of varnish: a clear straight-sided 8 oz drinking glass, 6.6 cm across and 10 cm tall, 0.30 kg with its contents, standing on the riser's top with its centre at (31, 0), on the riser's centreline 9 cm from the far end. Because of the pencil the riser rests on its left bottom edge and the pencil tip: its right bottom edge is 8 mm off the table, and the riser and the jar lean 7 degrees to the left. Distractors, not part of the task and ignored by scoring: (4) red ceramic mug, 9 cm across (11.4 cm with handle), 8 cm tall, 0.30 kg, at (48, +25), handle toward the arms; (5) roll of brown packing tape, 10 cm across, 5 cm tall, 0.06 kg, lying flat at (51, +12); (6) Phillips screwdriver, 19 cm long, 3.4 cm across the handle, 0.10 kg, lying left-right at x = 48 from y = -15 (handle end) to y = +4 (tip).
scoring: 0 if at any time the jar tilts more than 15 degrees from vertical (varnish over the rim) or leaves the riser's top face (the centre of its base outside the top's outline, or more than 1 cm off the face); putting things right afterwards does not undo this. Otherwise, judged at the end with the riser, jar and pencil all at rest: 1.0 if all four bottom corners of the riser are within 2 mm of the table, the riser's centre is within 1 cm of where it started and its long side within 5 degrees of straight away from the arms, the jar stands on the riser within 3 degrees of vertical, and, seen from above, no part of the pencil is within 2 cm of the riser. 0.5 if the riser is flat (same 2 mm test), the jar stands on it within 3 degrees of vertical and, seen from above, the pencil does not overlap the riser, but the riser's centre has moved more than 1 cm, or it has turned more than 5 degrees, or the pencil lies within 2 cm of it. 0 in every other case, including doing nothing, the pencil still under the riser or lying on it, a corner more than 2 mm off the table (as when the riser is still held up in a gripper), or the riser, jar or pencil still moving. A full score must hold for 3 s. The distractors are not scored.
reset_notes: Place the pencil first, then set the riser down with its right edge on the pencil tip, then stand the jar on it. Real trials can use water in the jar; wipe up any spill before the next trial.
fidelity: Rigid bodies under gravity and friction. The riser is a plain box primitive (its bottom corners stand in for feet) and the pencil a square-section bar primitive that cannot roll; the prop library used has no pencil. The jar is a SimReady drinking glass standing in for a jar; it is empty, collides as its convex hull (a solid shape), and its mass is set to 0.30 kg to stand for glass plus varnish. The varnish is not simulated: a tilt past 15 degrees at any moment counts as a spill, whatever the speed of the motion, and slopping from a jolt is not modelled. The mug, tape roll and screwdriver are SimReady props. Every surface has the same rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic), higher than wood on a real bench, so the pinned pencil drags the riser more readily than it would in reality, where it might instead slip out and let the riser drop 8 mm; even so the glass can creep up to about 1.5 cm across the leaning riser while the riser is handled. No force sensing; the scorer sees object poses only, not the grippers, so it cannot tell a released object from one held still.
